description: We are students from Poznan University of Technology. Our interests are software, microcontrollers and mechatronics.
summary:
We developed an interactive Astronaut Health Monitoring System designed to help astronauts monitor, assess, and improve their physical and mental wellbeing during long-duration space missions.

The application brings together health data in an accessible dashboard, allowing astronauts to track key indicators, analyze historical measurements, and compare results with other crew members to identify individual changes and broader health trends. It also includes manual telemetry logging and camera-based facial analysis to collect additional health-related information. To support cognitive health and engagement, we introduced reaction-time games and a crew leaderboard, encouraging friendly competition and social interaction.

A key feature is an AI-powered Medical Assistant that uses individual astronaut health records and medical literature to provide personalized, evidence-based guidance. The underlying medical sources are also accessible to astronauts, allowing them to independently verify the information.

Our solution aims to make health monitoring more accessible, engaging, and reliable, helping astronauts take an active role in maintaining their health throughout demanding space missions.
details:
Our project is an interactive Astronaut Health Monitoring System designed to support astronauts in monitoring and maintaining their physical and mental wellbeing during long-duration space missions.

The application provides several interconnected features. The Overview dashboard presents essential health information in one accessible place, while the Plots section allows users to analyze historical measurements and compare health indicators between crew members to identify individual changes or trends affecting the entire team. The Tests section enables manual telemetry input, including weight, hydration, and overall wellbeing, as well as camera-based facial analysis to assess indicators such as tiredness. The Activities section introduces reaction-time games and a crew leaderboard, turning health monitoring into a more engaging experience and encouraging friendly competition. Finally, an AI-powered Medical Assistant uses individual health records stored in the database and medical literature to provide personalized, evidence-based guidance. Astronauts can also access the referenced medical literature directly to independently verify the AI's responses.

The system was developed entirely in Python, using Streamlit to build the interactive user interface and SQLite as the database for storing and retrieving astronaut health data.

Our main creative approach was to combine health monitoring, data analysis, AI assistance, and gamification into a single platform. We considered the unique challenges of space missions, including limited access to medical assistance, isolation, and the importance of maintaining both physical and mental health. The intended impact is to encourage astronauts to take a more active role in their healthcare, recognize potential health changes early, and maintain a healthier and more supportive crew environment.
